test.title: Murray 3: long-crested, well-behaved waves (Gorge-like)
test.purpose: A narrow, long-crested sea (spread 5 degrees): the sim's groups last, and the next steep wave comes up about half a wavelength downwind of the last (in the sim: r 0.85 against 0.30 in the wind seas). Murray Stewart's cues (Rottnest camp, November 2026): catch a wave, as square as needed; stay high on its face (ease off, let the push hold you); scan 3 to 8 m ahead of the bow, within 30 degrees either side, for darker patches on the back faces ahead; when one is in reach, sprint to drop and move to it, to be on the upper part of the next wave's face there; prefer running diagonal to square.
lookFor: the next big face after a big one: half a wavelength on?
whether every place within reach is about as good (the crests are long)
questions: Does this match the Gorge, where the follow-up waves come half a wavelength further down?
Is aiming worth anything here, or only timing?
